newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Papua New Guinea names new military chief.
newsitem.headline: Papua New Guinea names new military chief.

text.p: Papua New Guinea on Wednesday appointed a controversial Australian-trained officer to head its small military, which mutinied recently over plans to use mercenaries to quash an island rebellion.

Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, who reclaimed his post this week after the army mutiny forced him to stand aside briefly, appointed Colonel Leo Nuia defence force chief and promoted him to Brigadier-General.
A military official told Reuters that Nuia, whose appointment was endorsed by cabinet, was sworn in at a special ceremony on Wednesday.

Nuia was sacked as the commander of the country's forces on Bougainville island, where rebels are fighting for independence, after publicly admitting in 1991 that the bodies of rebels had been dumped from Australian-supplied helicopters.
He also said the helicopters had been used as gunships, contravening condition Canberra had imposed on their use.
Nuia, who joined the army in 1967 and was trained at Australia's Portsea officers school, replaces Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok as head of the 4,000-strong military.

Singirok was sacked in March after criticising Chan's US$36 million plan to use mercenaries to end a nine-year revolt on Bougainville island in which thousands have died, mainly from disease and lack of medical care.
Singirok's sacking and the mercenary plan sparked a 10-day civil and military revolt, the worst in the South Pacific Nation's 22 years of independence.
Chan and two senior ministers were forced to stand aside pending the outcome of an inquiry into the deal.
Chan declared on Monday he was reclaiming his post, saying the recently-completed inquiry had cleared him of any wrongdoing.
But the situation remained confused ahead of elections due to start in 10 days, with caretaker prime minister John Giheno saying he remains in charge.
Papua New Guineans go to the polls on June 14, with voting expected to take about three weeks to complete.
